mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior 6-month average predicts a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened discount rates affecting expected cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-tightening mean (p > 0.05) in the tightening regime.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS rises above its 12-month moving average, labor market strength is interpreted as supportive of corporate earnings, driving a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant outperformance over the 12-month moving average baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in GDPC1 (real private demand) followed by a rebound above the 5-period low predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as market anticipates a resumption of growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative or flat during the identified recovery pattern (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls below its 3-month moving average, indicating softening supply conditions, S&P 20-day forward returns are expected to turn negative as market anticipates profit compression.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly below the 3-month average (p > 0.05) during the contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2-month decline in UNRATE accompanied by a rise in FEDFUNDS suggests conflicting policy signals, producing a negative S&P 5-day forward return as uncertainty increases.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified policy uncertainty episode.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (household utilization) exceeds its 4-week high, indicating overutilization, S&P 60-day forward returns are predicted to turn negative due to risk aversion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show a statistically significant negative deviation from the prior 4-week average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (real private savings) followed by a sustained rise above the prior 10-day average signals a shift from saving to spending, supporting equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 10-day average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) shows a 2% monthly increase above the prior month, indicating accelerating inflation, S&P 20-day forward returns are expected to turn negative due to rate hike anticipation.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior month (p > 0.05) during the inflation episode.
